note:
Close-up header banner candidates for /pages/our-philosophy. Malcolm, 2026-08-27, after seeing P1-graphite-woman-38-nbp_pro_01 live: bring the foreground woman's head MUCH closer, so you see from her eyes down to her smile.

CASTING IS FIXED, NOT FANNED. The previous wave varied four castings because nothing had been chosen; Malcolm has now chosen, so both slots carry the SAME woman as the published banner - about thirty-eight, north-western European, dark blonde in a low ponytail, no makeup. The variety in this wave comes from the six suppliers and from the two framing distances, not from the casting.

TWO DISTANCES, AND C2 IS INSURANCE RATHER THAN INDECISION. C1 is the framing asked for: eyes at the top, smile below the middle, forehead cut by the top edge. C2 pulls back by about one facial feature - brows to the base of the throat. C1 is the target; C2 exists because a 4.42:1 band has to be CUT from a 2.909:1 generation, so a candidate briefed to the exact final framing leaves no latitude at all, and cropping an eye or the smile off wastes the whole candidate. Every slot is briefed a little looser than the band it will become, and the band is aimed afterwards.

TWO NEGATIVE GUARDS HAD TO COME OUT, AND THAT IS THE RECURRING FAULT ON THIS PROJECT. The medium-shot wave carried 'no head touching the top edge, no head cropped by the top edge' - written to stop engines jamming the head against the top. This brief REQUIRES the forehead to be cut by the top edge. Leaving them in would have produced a wave that quietly refused the instruction with a prompt that read perfectly, which is the third time in one day the same shape has come up. Replaced with the opposite guards: no full face in frame, no headroom above the head, no head and shoulders portrait, no small face.

SKIN REALISM IS LOAD-BEARING AT THIS MAGNIFICATION. At eyes-to-smile the face fills most of an 848px band, so plastic skin is no longer a subtle fault - it is the whole picture. The skin paragraph is expanded to name pores, downy cheek hair, redness at the nostril and inner eye corner, and countable individual lashes and brow hairs.

LUMA GETS ITS OWN SHORTER BRIEF via prompt_luma - it caps prompts at 6000 characters and answers a longer one with a bare HTTP 422 that names neither length nor content.

slots.title: Eyes down to smile - the framing asked for
slots.prompt:
A photograph of one woman at work in a cosmetic-chemistry laboratory, taken on a full-frame camera with a fast 85mm lens wide open. The picture is a wide horizontal band, close to three times as wide as it is tall.

THE WHOLE PICTURE IS DARK. This is a laboratory lit low and deliberately: the dominant tone across the entire frame is GRAPHITE - a deep, neutral, very slightly cool near-black - and she is lit against it. Not a bright laboratory and not an airy one.

HOW CLOSE SHE IS - THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE PICTURE. Her head is very close to the camera and enormous in the frame. The picture runs FROM HER EYES DOWN TO HER SMILE: her eyes sit in the upper part of the frame and her smiling mouth sits below the middle. Her forehead is cut off by the top edge of the picture just above the eyebrows, and her chin, jaw and the top of her white collar fill the lower part of the frame. Both eyes, both brows, the whole nose, both cheeks and the whole smiling mouth are in view and none of them is cropped.

HER FACE IS ON THE RIGHT, NOT IN THE MIDDLE. The outer edge of her far cheek falls a little past the middle of the picture, and her face and hair fill the right side out to the right edge. The whole LEFT HALF of the picture is the laboratory behind her, going away from the camera into the dark.

WHO SHE IS: a woman of about thirty-eight, north-western European, with dark blonde hair pulled back into a low practical ponytail and a few strands loose at the temples. Light hazel eyes, straight brows, fair skin. She wears no makeup at all.

HER SKIN IS REAL AND UNRETOUCHED, AND AT THIS DISTANCE THAT IS EVERYTHING. Individual pores are visible across the nose, the cheeks and the chin. There are fine lines at the outer corners of both eyes that deepen as she smiles, and one faint line across what is left of the forehead. A scatter of small freckles crosses the nose and cheekbones, with two or three small moles. There is faint natural unevenness of colour beside the nose and along the jaw, a little redness at the nostril and the inner eye corner, fine downy hair catching the light on the cheek, and the ordinary sheen of real skin on the nose and cheekbone. Individual eyelashes and individual eyebrow hairs are separate and countable. Nothing is smoothed, evened, filled or airbrushed, and no beauty filter has been anywhere near this photograph.

SHE IS LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THE LENS AND SMILING. A genuine, warm, unforced smile that reaches her eyes and creases the skin at their outer corners, upper teeth just showing, lips relaxed, the cheeks lifted by the smile. Not a wide grin, not a laugh, not a held pose - the expression of someone who has glanced up at a colleague she likes. Her eyes are sharp, alive and directed at the camera, with a soft catchlight in each.

A SECOND PERSON WORKS FAR BEHIND HER, DEEPLY OUT OF FOCUS. A man in a plain white laboratory coat sits at a bench a long way back on the LEFT side of the picture, side-on to the camera and bent forward with both eyes to the eyepieces of a microscope. His head is down at the instrument, so his face is not visible and never turns to the camera. He is so far outside the plane of focus that he reads as a soft pale shape with no facial detail whatsoever - unmistakably a second person working at a microscope, but never a second portrait. At this magnification he is small and dim, and he does not overlap her.

ONLY SHE IS SHARP. The plane of focus falls on her eyes, and the depth of field is so shallow that it is already softening at her ear. Everything behind her dissolves completely: the colleague at the microscope is very soft indeed, and the far side of the room is entirely unreadable - shapes, tone and light only, with not one legible edge, not one identifiable object and nothing written anywhere. Points of light far behind her open into smooth round discs.

THE ROOM, WHICH FILLS THE WHOLE LEFT SIDE AND REACHES EVERY EDGE OF THE PICTURE: a modern cosmetic-chemistry laboratory kept deliberately dark. Charcoal-graphite cabinetry, a near-black slate worktop, dark walls, and deep shadow through most of the depth of the room. Far back there are a few cool blue-white sources - a strip of light under a cabinet, the pale glow of a screen turned away from the camera, light catching the shoulder of tall glassware - which read as soft rounded pools of light rather than as objects. There are also one or two very small copper-coloured pinpoints of light very deep in the background, no bigger than a coin would look at that distance, and nothing else in the picture is warm. The room continues past the left edge, past the top edge and past the bottom edge. Dim but never murky: there is real depth, separation and detail in the shadow rather than a flat black wall, and no part of the frame is a plain flat field of a single colour.

LIGHT AND COLOUR: a single cool key light from her front left puts clean daylight-coloured light across her face, with soft shadow under the cheekbone and the jaw and a soft catchlight in each eye. She is by a clear margin the brightest thing in the picture. The palette is graphite, dark teal and cool blue-white, with only those few tiny copper points. No overall warm cast, no golden light, no orange, no tungsten glow.

It looks like a real photograph of a real working scientist, taken by a good photographer on an ordinary working day.
